mainTopic: איוב's suffering: the שטן's role, whether איוב sinned, and ה׳'s answer from the storm
overview: The amud goes through the story of איוב's suffering. First it quotes the פסוקים about his last disasters and how he still blessed ה׳. Next comes the scene in heaven: the שטן praises אברהם's faith, ה׳ praises איוב, and רבי יוחנן remarks how bold it is to say that ה׳ was 'persuaded.' The גמרא then talks about the שטן himself. A ברייתא lists his three jobs, ריש לקיש says the שטן, the יצר הרע and the מלאך המות are one, and רבי לוי says the שטן and פנינה both acted לשם שמים. Next comes a debate about whether איוב sinned in his heart. רבא and רבי אליעזר say he did, while אביי and רבי יהושע say he was speaking about the שטן. The גמרא also brings איוב's claim that people cannot be blamed for their deeds, and his friends' answer that the תורה is the cure for the יצר הרע. It praises איוב's kindness to orphans and widows, but it also criticizes several things he said. Last, it explains how ה׳ answered איוב 'from the storm': He takes exact care of every hair, raindrop and thunderclap, and that explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Closing words: a taste of the World to Come
steps.stepSummary: The last words of the previous explanation: what happened on איוב's land was like עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: …a taste of the World to Come.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the thought from the end of the last section. It says that what happened in איוב's fields was a small taste of עולם הבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line belongs to the explanation that came just before. It is not a new idea. It closes that point so that the גמרא can go back to reading the פסוקים in order.

phrases.english: a taste of the World to Come.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the explanation from the previous section.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The miracle on איוב's land was like a small taste of עולם הבא.

steps.title: The remaining disasters, and how Job reacts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes איוב 1:16–22. Messengers arrive one after another to report fire, raiders and a deadly wind, and איוב still blesses ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: While one messenger was still speaking, another came and said: The fire of God fell, and so on. While he was still speaking, another came and said: The Chaldeans formed three bands, raided the camels and took them, and so on. While he was still speaking, another came and said: Your sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine in their oldest brother's house. A great wind came from across the desert, struck the four corners of the house, and it fell on the young people, and so on. Then איוב got up, tore his coat, shaved his head, and so on. He said: Naked I came out of my mother's womb, and naked I will return there. ה׳ gave and ה׳ took; may the name of ה׳ be blessed. In all this איוב did not sin, and he did not speak wrongly against God.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps reading the פסוקים of איוב in order. Here they describe the last of the disasters and איוב's response.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bad news comes in a nonstop stream, with each messenger arriving before the last one has finished speaking. Even so, איוב mourns and still blesses ה׳. The פסוק itself says that he did not sin. This is the starting point for the discussion that follows about whether איוב really stayed faithful.

keyTerms.meaning: while this one was still speaking
'and so on'; the rest of the פסוק is left out
he tore his coat, a sign of mourning
something improper; a complaint against God

steps.whyThisMatters: The line 'ה׳ gave and ה׳ took' is the classic model of accepting suffering. The claim that איוב did not sin is what the next part of the story will test.

phrases.english: "While this one was still speaking, another came,
and said: The fire of God, etc.
phrases.notes: איוב 1:16. 'וְגוֹ׳' means 'and so on,' so the גמרא is cutting the פסוק short.

phrases.english: While this one was still speaking, another came,
and said: The Chaldeans formed three bands,
and they raided the camels and took them, etc.
While this one was still speaking, another came,

phrases.aramaic: וַיֹּאמַר: בָּנֶיךָ וּבְנוֹתֶיךָ אוֹכְלִים וְשׁוֹתִים יַיִן
phrases.english: and said: Your sons and your daughters were eating and drinking wine
in the house of their oldest brother,

phrases.aramaic: וְהִנֵּה רוּחַ גְּדוֹלָה בָּאָה מֵעֵבֶר הַמִּדְבָּר,
phrases.english: and suddenly a great wind came from across the desert,
and struck the four corners of the house,
and it fell on the young people, etc.
Then Job got up and tore his coat,
and shaved his head, etc.,
and he said: Naked I came out of my mother's womb,
and naked I will return there;
the Lord gave and the Lord took,
may the name of the Lord be blessed.
In all this, Job did not sin,
and he did not speak anything improper against God."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues reading the פסוקים of איוב after finishing the previous explanation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even after losing everything, איוב blessed ה׳ and did not sin.

steps.title: The Satan reports that he has been roaming the earth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes איוב 2:1–2. The heavenly beings gather, ה׳ asks the שטן where he has come from, and he answers, 'From roaming the earth.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And there was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves, and so on. ה׳ said to the שטן: Where have you come from? The שטן answered ה׳ and said: From roaming the earth, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the opening of איוב perek 2. This is a setup step: the words 'from roaming the earth' are about to be explained in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On their own, these פסוקים just set the scene in heaven. The גמרא quotes them in order to fill in what the שטן meant by 'roaming the earth.' It will do that right away.

keyTerms.meaning: the sons of God; heavenly beings
to present themselves; to stand before

phrases.aramaic: וַיְהִי הַיּוֹם, וַיָּבֹאוּ בְּנֵי הָאֱלֹהִים לְהִתְיַצֵּב וְגוֹ׳.
phrases.english: "And there was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves, etc.
phrases.notes: איוב 2:1

phrases.aramaic: וַיֹּאמֶר ה׳ אֶל הַשָּׂטָן: אֵי מִזֶּה תָּבֹא?
phrases.english: And the Lord said to the Satan: Where have you come from?
And the Satan answered the Lord,
and said: From roaming the earth, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: וַיְהִי הַיּוֹם וַיָּבֹאוּ בְּנֵי הָאֱלֹהִים לְהִתְיַצֵּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from perek 1 to perek 2 of איוב and sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק records that the שטן said he came 'from roaming the earth.'

steps.title: The Satan praises Abraham's faith
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the שטן's words. He searched the whole world and found no one like אברהם, who was promised the land but could not find a place to bury שרה, and still did not question ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said before Him: Master of the World, I have roamed the whole world and have not found anyone like Your servant אברהם. You told him: 'Get up, walk through the land, its length and its width, because I will give it to you.' Yet when he wanted to bury שרה, he could not find a place to bury her, and he did not question Your ways.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fills in what the שטן was really saying when he answered 'from roaming the earth.' He reported that אברהם's faith was unmatched anywhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point rests on a contrast. ה׳ promised אברהם the entire land, yet אברהם did not own even a burial plot for שרה. Even so, he did not complain that the promise had not been kept. This praise of אברהם sets up ה׳'s reply about איוב.

keyTerms.meaning: he did not question Your ways

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the standard that איוב will be measured against: accepting ה׳'s ways even when a promise seems not to come true.

phrases.english: He said before Him: Master of the World,
I have roamed through the whole world,
and I have not found anyone like Your servant Abraham,
to whom You said:
"Get up, walk through the land, its length and its width,
phrases.notes: בראשית 13:17

phrases.english: because I will give it to you,"
and when he wanted to bury Sarah,
he did not find a place to bury her,
and still he did not question Your ways.
phrases.notes: He means that אברהם never complained that ה׳'s promise of the land had not been kept.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְפָנָיו רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם שַׁטְתִּי בְּכׇל הָעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the words 'from roaming the earth' quoted in the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שטן found no one as faithful as אברהם, who did not question ה׳ even when the promise of the land seemed unfulfilled.

steps.title: God answers: Have you noticed My servant Job?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes איוב 2:3. ה׳ answers the שטן by praising איוב, who is still holding on to his innocence even though he was struck for no reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: And ה׳ said to the שטן: Have you paid attention to My servant איוב, that there is no one like him on earth, and so on? He is still holding on to his innocence, and you persuaded Me against him to destroy him for nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes ה׳'s reply to the שטן. This is a setup step: the גמרא is about to explain this פסוק, especially the hard words 'you persuaded Me against him.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read together with the previous step, ה׳ is pointing out that איוב is like אברהם: he is also staying faithful through suffering. The phrase 'you persuaded Me to destroy him for nothing' is a very surprising thing to say about ה׳. Step 6 deals with it.

keyTerms.meaning: have you paid attention; have you noticed
holding on to his innocence or integrity
and you persuaded Me; you stirred Me up

steps.confusionAlert: This step is not the גמרא's conclusion. The line ends with a dash because the גמרא's explanation of this פסוק comes right after it.

phrases.english: "And the Lord said to the Satan:
Have you paid attention to My servant Job,
phrases.notes: איוב 2:3

phrases.english: that there is no one like him on earth, etc.,
and he is still holding on to his innocence,
and you persuaded Me against him, to destroy him for nothing."

steps.triggerLanguage: וַיֹּאמֶר ה׳ אֶל הַשָּׂטָן הֲשַׂמְתָּ לִבְּךָ אֶל עַבְדִּי אִיּוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: ה׳'s reply to the שטן's praise of אברהם; it sets up the next explanation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳ praises איוב as unmatched on earth and still faithful despite being struck for no reason.

steps.title: Only a verse could say ה׳ was persuaded
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן comments on the words 'you persuaded Me against him' from the פסוק just quoted. If the פסוק did not say it, no one could dare say it: it makes ה׳ sound like a person who lets others talk him into things.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: If the פסוק did not say it, we could never say it. It sounds like a person whom others talk into something, and he goes along with it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן reacts to a bold phrase in the פסוק from step 5. He says the words are so daring that we could only say them because the פסוק says them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 5, ה׳ tells the שטן, 'you persuaded Me against him.' Taken simply, this sounds as if ה׳ was talked into harming איוב. רבי יוחנן points out how daring this is: we may only say it because it is written.

keyTerms.meaning: Were it not that / if not for
It would be impossible to say it

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says:
Were it not that the verse is written,
it would be impossible to say it:
like a person whom others persuade, and he lets himself be persuaded.
phrases.notes: He's talking about the words 'you persuaded Me against him' from איוב 2:3, which the גמרא quoted just before.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אִלְמָלֵא מִקְרָא כָּתוּב, אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְאוֹמְרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Comments on a phrase in the פסוק quoted in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The idea that ה׳ was 'persuaded' could only be said because the פסוק says it.

steps.title: The שטן's three-part method
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא describes what the שטן does. He comes down and leads a person to sin. He goes up and stirs up anger against him. Then he gets permission and takes the person's soul.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: He comes down and leads people astray. He goes up and stirs up anger. He takes permission, and he takes the soul.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the story is about the שטן, the גמרא brings a ברייתא that describes his three jobs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא shows a full cycle. First the שטן tempts a person to sin. Then he accuses that person in heaven. Then he carries out the punishment. This prepares for ריש לקיש's teaching later in step 10.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita:
He goes down and leads astray,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the שטן. The ברייתא doesn't name him, but that's who we're talking about.

phrases.english: and goes up and stirs up anger,
takes permission, and takes the soul.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ברייתא about the שטן, who is persuading ה׳ in the story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שטן tempts, then accuses, then gets permission and takes the soul.

steps.title: The second test: the שטן may strike איוב's body
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the פסוקים. The שטן says a person will give anything to save his own life, so he asks to strike איוב's body. ה׳ allows it but tells him to spare איוב's life, and the שטן strikes איוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: The שטן answered ה׳: 'Skin for skin. A man will give everything he has for his life. But touch his bones and flesh, and he will curse You to Your face.' ה׳ said: 'He is in your hand, only guard his life.' The שטן went out and struck איוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to quoting the book of איוב. Here the שטן asks to test איוב a second time, now with pain in his own body. This sets up the comments that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שטן argues that losing his property and children was not a real test, because a person cares most about his own body. ה׳ allows the test, with one limit: איוב's life must be kept. That limit becomes the key to the next two teachings.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'will bless You'; a polite way of saying 'will curse You'

phrases.english: "And the Satan answered the Lord and said:
phrases.notes: איוב 2:4–7

phrases.english: Skin for skin,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֹל אֲשֶׁר לָאִישׁ יִתֵּן בְּעַד נַפְשׁוֹ.
phrases.english: and all that a man has he will give for his life.
But send forth Your hand now
and touch his bone and his flesh,
and he will surely 'bless' You to Your face.
phrases.notes: 'Bless' here is a polite way of saying 'curse'. The פסוק avoids writing that word about ה׳.

phrases.english: And the Lord said to the Satan:

phrases.aramaic: הִנּוֹ בְיָדֶךָ, אַךְ אֶת נַפְשׁוֹ שְׁמֹר.
phrases.english: Behold, he is in your hand; only guard his life.
And the Satan went out from before the Lord,
and struck Job, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: וַיַּעַן הַשָּׂטָן אֶת ה׳ וַיֹּאמַר: עוֹר בְּעַד עוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the פסוקים, continuing right after the פסוק quoted in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳ lets the שטן strike איוב's body, but not take his life.

steps.title: The שטן suffered more than איוב
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק says the שטן's job was harder than איוב's pain. It was like a servant told to break a barrel without spilling the wine: he had to hurt איוב badly while still keeping him alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק says: The שטן suffered more than איוב. It is like a servant whose master told him: 'Break the barrel, but save the wine.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק comments on the limit ה׳ set: hurt איוב, but guard his life. He explains it with a short parable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Breaking a barrel and saving its wine at the same time is almost impossible. In the same way, the שטן had to strike איוב hard while making sure he did not die. That limit made the task very hard for the שטן.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak says:
The suffering of the Satan was harder
than that of Job.
A parable: a servant whose master said to him:
Break the barrel, but save its wine.
phrases.notes: This matches the order the שטן got: strike איוב's body, but keep his life safe.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: קָשֶׁה צַעֲרוֹ שֶׁל שָׂטָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Comments on the limit 'only guard his life' from step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because of the limit ה׳ set, the שטן's task was harder than איוב's suffering.

steps.title: The שטן, the יצר הרע and the מלאך המות are one
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש teaches that three things are really one: the שטן, the יצר הרע and the מלאך המות.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש says: He is the שטן, he is the יצר הרע, and he is the מלאך המות.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש makes a big claim: three forces that seem different are actually the same one. The next three steps bring a proof for each part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits the ברייתא in step 7. The one who tempts is the יצר הרע, the one who accuses is the שטן, and the one who takes the soul is the מלאך המות. ריש לקיש says all three are the same.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish says:
He is the Satan, he is the evil inclination,
he is the Angel of Death.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: הוּא שָׂטָן, הוּא יֵצֶר הָרָע, הוּא מַלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the ברייתא's three roles and the פסוקים about the שטן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שטן, the יצר הרע and the מלאך המות are one being.

steps.title: Proof that he is the שטן
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש proves the first part from the פסוק that calls him 'the שטן' as he goes out from before ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is the שטן, as it says: 'And the שטן went out from before ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the first of three proofs for ריש לקיש's claim. It shows that this being is called 'the שטן'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This part is simple: the פסוק itself calls him 'השטן'. It sets the starting point, and the next two proofs link this same being to the other two names.

phrases.english: He is the Satan:
as it is written: "And the Satan went out from before the Lord."
phrases.notes: איוב 2:7, the same פסוק the גמרא quoted a moment ago.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the first part of ריש לקיש's claim.
steps.raayaObject: That this being is the שטן.

steps.title: Proof that he is the יצר הרע
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש links the word 'רק' (only) in two פסוקים. One is about the evil thoughts of a person's heart, and one is about the שטן in איוב. The shared word shows that the שטן and the יצר הרע are the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is the יצר הרע. It says there: 'only evil all the day,' and it says here: 'only upon him do not send your hand.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second proof. It connects the שטן to the יצר הרע through the shared word 'רק'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In בראשית, 'רק' describes the evil thoughts of the heart, which is the יצר הרע. In איוב, 'רק' appears in ה׳'s words to the שטן. Because the same word appears in both, ריש לקיש links the two and says they are one being.

phrases.english: He is the evil inclination:
It is written there: "only evil all the day,"
phrases.notes: בראשית 6:5

phrases.english: and it is written here:
("only guard his life")
phrases.notes: The words in round brackets are in the standard printed גמרא, but the corrected wording leaves them out. The words in the square brackets that follow replace them.

phrases.english: ["only upon him do not send your hand"].
phrases.notes: איוב 1:12. It uses the same word 'רק' as the פסוק in בראשית.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא יֵצֶר הָרָע – כְּתִיב הָתָם: ״רַק רַע כׇּל הַיּוֹם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the second part of ריש לקיש's claim.
steps.raayaObject: That the שטן is the יצר הרע.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The word 'רק' in בראשית 6:5 and איוב 1:12.

steps.title: Proof that he is the מלאך המות
steps.stepSummary: ה׳ had to tell the שטן to guard איוב's life. That shows איוב's life was in the שטן's hands, so the שטן must also be the מלאך המות.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is the מלאך המות, as it says: 'Only guard his life.' This shows that איוב's life depended on him.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the third and last proof. It shows that the שטן also has the power to take life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ה׳ would only need to say 'guard his life' if the שטן was able to take it. So the power over death belongs to the שטן, and he is the מלאך המות. This completes ריש לקיש's claim that all three are one.

keyTerms.meaning: It depends on him; it is in his hands

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש teaches that the שטן, the יצר הרע and the מלאך המות are one being. He proves each part from a פסוק: the name 'השטן', the shared word 'רק', and the order to 'guard his life'.

phrases.english: He is the Angel of Death:
as it is written: "(only) [only] guard his life":
phrases.notes: איוב 2:6. Some versions say 'רק' (round brackets), but the corrected wording in square brackets says 'אך', like the פסוק itself.

phrases.english: evidently it depends on him.
phrases.notes: 'It' means איוב's life.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the third and final part of ריש לקיש's claim.
steps.raayaObject: That the שטן is the מלאך המות.

steps.title: The שטן and פנינה both meant well
steps.stepSummary: רבי לוי teaches that both the שטן and פנינה had good intentions, לשם שמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי לוי said: The שטן and פנינה both meant it for the sake of Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי לוי makes a surprising new claim: two characters who caused pain, the שטן and פנינה, actually had good intentions. The next two steps will explain each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the שטן looked like the one who hurt איוב and who is even the מלאך המות. רבי לוי adds that his reason for accusing איוב was לשם שמים. He also puts פנינה, who hurt חנה, in the same group.

keyTerms.meaning: For the sake of Heaven; with a good, holy purpose
The other wife of אֶלְקָנָה, who upset חַנָּה

phrases.english: Rabbi Levi said:
The Satan and Peninnah
phrases.notes: פנינה was חנה's rival wife. חנה became the mother of שמואל.

phrases.english: intended it for the sake of Heaven.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי לֵוִי: שָׂטָן וּפְנִינָה לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם נִתְכַּוְּונוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from who the שטן is to what his intentions were
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both the שטן and פנינה acted לשם שמים.

steps.title: Why the שטן's intention was good
steps.stepSummary: The שטן saw ה׳ favoring איוב and worried that ה׳'s love for אברהם would be forgotten.
steps.simpleTranslation: The שטן: when he saw that הקדוש ברוך הוא was leaning toward איוב, he said: Heaven forbid that He should forget His love for אברהם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first half of רבי לוי's claim, about the שטן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שטן did not accuse איוב out of hatred. He saw ה׳ praising איוב highly and worried this would push aside the special love for אברהם. So he tested איוב to protect אברהם's place.

keyTerms.meaning: His mind leaned toward; He favored

phrases.english: The Satan:
once he saw the Holy One, Blessed be He,
that His mind was leaning toward Job,
he said: Heaven forbid
that He should forget His love for Abraham.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׂטָן – כֵּיוָן דְּחַזְיֵא לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the שטן half of רבי לוי's claim
steps.raayaObject: That the שטן acted לשם שמים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The שטן's concern for the love of אברהם

steps.title: Why פנינה's intention was good
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק says פנינה upset חנה 'so that she would cry out,' which shows she had a good purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: פנינה: as it is written: 'And her rival made her very angry, in order to make her cry out.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports the second half of רבי לוי's claim from a פסוק about פנינה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'בעבור הרעימה' (in order to make her cry out) show that פנינה had a goal. She was not upsetting חנה just to hurt her. She wanted to stir חנה to cry out to ה׳.

keyTerms.meaning: In order to make her cry out or thunder

phrases.english: Peninnah: as it is written:
'And her rival made her very angry,'
phrases.notes: שמואל א 1:6

phrases.english: 'in order to make her cry out.'
phrases.notes: רבי לוי reads this as פנינה having a purpose: to stir חנה to cry out to ה׳.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the פנינה half of רבי לוי's claim

steps.title: The שטן thanks the one who taught this
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב taught this idea in פפוניא, and the שטן came and kissed his feet.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב taught this in פפוניא. The שטן came and kissed his feet.
steps.whatsHappening: A short story closes this idea: when רב אחא בר יעקב taught that the שטן meant well, the שטן came and kissed his feet in thanks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story shows the שטן was glad someone spoke well of him. It adds no new law. It shows how strongly the teaching defended his intentions.

phrases.aramaic: דַּרְשַׁהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב בְּפַפּוֹנְיָא.
phrases.english: Rav Aha bar Yaakov taught it publicly in Paphunya.
phrases.notes: 'It' means רבי לוי's teaching that the שטן meant well.

phrases.english: The Satan came and kissed his feet.

steps.triggerLanguage: דַּרְשַׁהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב בְּפַפּוֹנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story that caps רבי לוי's teaching
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שטן was grateful for being described as acting לשם שמים.

steps.title: איוב did not sin with his lips, but did in his heart
steps.stepSummary: רבא reads 'with his lips he did not sin' to mean איוב did sin in his heart.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'In all this איוב did not sin with his lips.' רבא said: With his lips he did not sin, but in his heart he did sin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic about איוב himself. רבא reads the פסוק closely: it says only that איוב did not sin with his lips.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could have just said 'איוב did not sin.' Because it adds 'with his lips,' רבא learns that his heart was a different story. Inside, he had wrong thoughts.

keyTerms.meaning: With his lips; in his speech
In his heart; in his thoughts

steps.confusionAlert: רבא does not say איוב said anything sinful out loud here. His point is about איוב's inner thoughts, which the next steps try to uncover from his words.

phrases.english: 'In all this Job did not sin with his lips.'
phrases.notes: איוב 2:10

phrases.english: Rava said:
With his lips he did not sin; in his heart he did sin.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּכׇל זֹאת לֹא חָטָא אִיּוֹב בִּשְׂפָתָיו. אָמַר רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new discussion about איוב's own behavior
steps.mimraCoreRuling: איוב sinned in his heart, though not with his lips.

steps.title: What did איוב say that shows this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which words of איוב show the thoughts in his heart.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was he saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question to set up the next step: which words of איוב reveal his wrong thoughts?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If איוב's sin was hidden in his heart, we need some sign of it. The גמרא is looking for a פסוק where his words hint at what he was thinking.

phrases.english: What was he saying?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for evidence of רבא's claim
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which words of איוב reveal the sin in his heart

steps.title: 'The earth is given into the hand of the wicked'
steps.stepSummary: רבא points to איוב's words 'the earth is given into the hand of the wicked' and says איוב wanted to turn the bowl upside down.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The earth is given into the hand of the wicked; he covers the faces of its judges; if not he, then who is it?' רבא said: איוב wanted to turn the bowl upside down.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer: in this פסוק, איוב hints that the world is run by a 'wicked one.' רבא calls this trying to turn the bowl upside down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא understands the 'wicked one' who controls the earth as a hint toward ה׳. That would be a terrible thought, so איוב only hinted at it. This shows the sin in his heart.

keyTerms.meaning: The earth is given into the hand of the wicked
To turn the bowl upside down; to speak against ה׳

phrases.english: 'The earth is given into the hand of the wicked;'
'he covers the faces of its judges;'
'if not he, then who is it?'
phrases.notes: איוב 9:24

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: בִּקֵּשׁ אִיּוֹב לַהֲפוֹךְ קְעָרָה עַל פִּיהָ.
phrases.english: Job wanted to turn the bowl upside down.
phrases.notes: A picture of flipping everything over. איוב was hinting at something against ה׳ without saying it outright.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: איוב's words 'the earth is given into the hand of the wicked' hint at a thought against ה׳.

steps.title: אביי: איוב meant the שטן
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that the 'wicked one' in איוב's words is the שטן, not ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: איוב spoke only about the שטן.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי rejects רבא's reading: the 'wicked one' איוב complained about was the שטן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the 'wicked one' is the שטן, then איוב said nothing against ה׳. So this פסוק is no proof of a sin in איוב's heart. This fits the earlier steps, where ה׳ handed איוב over to the שטן ('he is in your hand').

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Job did not speak
except about the Satan.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: לֹא דִּבֵּר אִיּוֹב אֶלָּא כְּנֶגֶד הַשָּׂטָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's reading of the פסוק
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from איוב 9:24 that איוב sinned in his heart
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The 'wicked one' can be read as the שטן, not ה׳.

steps.title: The same argument among the תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע argued the same way that רבא and אביי did.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like a dispute of the תנאים: 'The earth is given into the hand of the wicked.' רבי אליעזר says: איוב wanted to turn the bowl upside down. רבי יהושע said to him: איוב spoke only about the שטן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notes that the argument between רבא and אביי already existed between two תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר holds like רבא: איוב hinted at something against ה׳. רבי יהושע holds like אביי: איוב was talking about the שטן. So each אמורא has a תנא to rely on.
steps.whatToRemember: Whether איוב spoke against ה׳ in 'ארץ נתנה ביד רשע' is an open argument: רבא and רבי אליעזר say yes, אביי and רבי יהושע say he meant the שטן.

phrases.english: This is like a dispute of the Tannaim:
'The earth is given into the hand of the wicked.'
Rabbi Eliezer says:

phrases.aramaic: בִּקֵּשׁ אִיּוֹב לַהֲפוֹךְ קְעָרָה עַל פִּיהָ.
phrases.english: Job wanted to turn the bowl upside down.
Rabbi Yehoshua said to him:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא דִּבֵּר אִיּוֹב אֶלָּא כְּלַפֵּי שָׂטָן.
phrases.english: Job spoke only about the Satan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the רבא and אביי argument matches a dispute of תנאים
steps.raayaObject: That both רבא's and אביי's readings have earlier support
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with the dispute of רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע

steps.title: איוב tried to free the whole world from judgment
steps.stepSummary: From the פסוק 'You know I am not wicked, and no one can save from Your hand,' רבא says איוב tried to free everyone from judgment.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Although You know that I am not wicked, and there is no one who can save from Your hand.' רבא said: איוב wanted to free the whole world from judgment.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a second saying of איוב and explains it as a claim that no one should be judged.
steps.deeperAnalysis: איוב says it is all in ה׳'s hand and no one can escape it. רבא hears in this a bigger claim: if everything is controlled by ה׳, people cannot be held responsible. The next step spells out איוב's argument.

phrases.english: 'Although You know that I am not wicked,'
'and there is no one who can save from Your hand.'
phrases.notes: איוב 10:7

phrases.english: Rava said:
Job wanted to exempt

phrases.aramaic: אֶת כׇּל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ מִן הַדִּין.
phrases.english: the entire world from judgment.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל דַּעְתְּךָ כִּי לֹא אֶרְשָׁע וְאֵין מִיָּדְךָ מַצִּיל. אָמַר רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second example of איוב's harsh words, again explained by רבא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: איוב tried to free the whole world from judgment.

steps.title: איוב's argument: You created everything both ways
steps.stepSummary: איוב argues that ה׳ created kosher and non-kosher, גן עדן and גיהנם, צדיקים and רשעים, so who can stop Him?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said before Him: רבונו של עולם, You created the ox with split hooves, You created the donkey with closed hooves. You created גן עדן, You created גיהנם. You created צדיקים, You created רשעים. Who can stop You?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out איוב's argument for freeing the world from judgment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as an ox is born kosher and a donkey is born non-kosher, איוב claims people are created righteous or wicked. If ה׳ made them that way, איוב argues, they should not be punished for it. 'Who can stop You' means no one can push back against how ה׳ made them.

keyTerms.meaning: His hooves are split (a sign of a kosher animal)
The place of punishment after death

steps.whyThisMatters: This is איוב's complaint against free choice. It sets up the answer that comes next in the גמרא.

phrases.english: He said before Him: Master of the World,
You created the ox with split hooves,
You created the donkey with closed hooves;
You created Gan Eden, You created Gehinnom;
You created righteous people, You created wicked people.
Who can stop You?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the reasoning behind רבא's claim in step 23
steps.raayaObject: That איוב wanted to free the world from judgment
steps.raayaSupportSource: איוב's comparison of people to animals born kosher or non-kosher

steps.title: איוב's friends answer that the Torah is the cure for the evil inclination
steps.stepSummary: איוב's friends answer him: yes, ה׳ created the יצר הרע, but He also created the תורה to balance it, so people are not trapped.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did איוב's friends answer him? 'You do away with fear of God and weaken prayer before Him.' ה׳ created the יצר הרע, but He also created the תורה as its cure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the friends' reply to איוב's claim from Step 24 that ה׳ made רשעים, so no one can be blamed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: איוב argued that people are not responsible, because ה׳ created both good and evil. The friends answer that ה׳ also gave a cure, the תורה, so a person can beat his יצר הרע. That means the person is still responsible for his choices.

keyTerms.meaning: you do away with fear of God
spice, here meaning a cure that balances something

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic idea in Jewish thought: the יצר הרע is real, but the תורה gives a person the power to overcome it, so people are still responsible for what they do.

phrases.english: And what did his friends [of איוב] answer him?
phrases.notes: The square-bracket word just makes it clear whose friends these are.

phrases.english: "You too do away with fear of God,
phrases.notes: איוב 15:4

phrases.english: and lessen prayer before God";

phrases.aramaic: בָּרָא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא יֵצֶר הָרָע –
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, created the evil inclination,
but He created the Torah as its antidote.
phrases.notes: Literally 'spice.' The תורה is what balances and fixes the יצר הרע.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers איוב's argument from Step 24 that ה׳ created רשעים, so no one can stop Him.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What did איוב's friends say back to him?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ה׳ created the יצר הרע but also created the תורה as its cure, so people stay responsible.

steps.title: רבא explains איוב's kindness to orphans and widows
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains a פסוק about איוב: he took orphans' fields, improved them, and gave them back, and he helped unmarried widows find husbands.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא taught: What does it mean, 'The blessing of the lost one came on me, and I made the widow's heart sing'? 'The blessing of the lost one' teaches that איוב would take a field from orphans, improve it, and give it back to them. 'I made the widow's heart sing' means that wherever there was a widow no one would marry, he would go and attach his name to her, and then people would come and marry her.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains two halves of a פסוק in which איוב describes his own good deeds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each half of the פסוק is explained by a specific act. The orphans 'lost' their field for a while but got it back in better condition, so they blessed him. With widows, his name made them look desirable, so someone married them.

keyTerms.meaning: the blessing of the one who was lost
casts his name on her (links his name to her)

steps.confusionAlert: The word 'stole' sounds bad, but here איוב took the field only to improve it and give it back. רבא is describing a kindness.

phrases.english: Rava expounded: What is the meaning of what is written:
"The blessing of the one who was lost came upon me,
phrases.notes: איוב 29:13

phrases.english: and I made the widow's heart sing"?
"The blessing of the one who was lost came upon me":
this teaches that he would take a field from orphans,
improve it, and give it back to them.
"And I made the widow's heart sing":
for wherever there was a widow
whom people would not marry,
he would go and cast his name upon her,
phrases.notes: He would let people think she was connected to him, so she would seem a good match.

phrases.english: and then people would come and marry her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the argument with איוב to a separate teaching that praises איוב's good deeds.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: איוב improved orphans' fields and gave them back, and he helped unwanted widows get married.

steps.title: רב criticizes איוב for weighing himself against Heaven
steps.stepSummary: איוב wished his suffering could be weighed on a scale. רב says he should not have said it, because it treats Heaven like an equal partner.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'If only my anger were weighed, and my calamity lifted together on the scales.' רב said: Dust in איוב's mouth! Can one act like a friend and equal toward Heaven?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא begins a list of things איוב said that חז״ל criticize. This is the first one, from רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting yourself and ה׳ on two sides of one scale treats you as His equal. רב says this was disrespectful.

keyTerms.meaning: dust in his mouth (he should not have said it)

phrases.english: "If only my anger were truly weighed,
phrases.notes: איוב 6:2

phrases.english: and my calamity lifted together on the scales":
Rav said: Dust in the mouth of איוב!
phrases.notes: A sharp way of saying 'he never should have said that.'

phrases.english: Is there friendship as equals toward Heaven?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After praising איוב in Step 26, the גמרא now turns to criticizing things he said.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: איוב should not have spoken as if he and Heaven were equals on a scale.

steps.title: רב criticizes איוב for wanting a judge over ה׳
steps.stepSummary: איוב wished there were a judge between himself and ה׳. רב says a servant cannot rebuke his master.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'If only there were someone to judge between us, who could lay his hand on us both.' רב said: Dust in איוב's mouth! Is there a servant who rebukes his master?
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second criticism in the list, again from רב, about another פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Asking for a judge over both of them treats ה׳ like an equal party in a court case. רב answers that a person is ה׳'s servant, and a servant does not argue his master into court.

phrases.english: "If only there were a judge between us,
phrases.notes: איוב 9:33

phrases.english: who could lay his hand upon us both":
Rav said: Dust in the mouth of איוב!

phrases.aramaic: כְּלוּם יֵשׁ עֶבֶד שֶׁמּוֹכִיחַ אֶת רַבּוֹ?!
phrases.english: Is there a servant who rebukes his master?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second criticism in the same pattern as Step 27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person cannot ask for a judge over ה׳, just as a servant cannot rebuke his master.

steps.title: רבא shows that אברהם was more careful with his eyes than איוב
steps.stepSummary: איוב boasted that he never looked at a young woman. רבא says this was nothing special, because אברהם did not even look at his own wife, and he proves it from a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'I made a covenant with my eyes, so how could I look at a young woman?' רבא said: Dust in איוב's mouth! He did not look at other women, but אברהם did not even look at his own wife, as it says, 'Now I know that you are a beautiful woman.' This shows that before then he did not know.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the third criticism. רבא compares איוב to אברהם and proves his point from a פסוק in בראשית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: איוב was proud that he avoided looking at women who were not his. רבא shows that אברהם went further and did not even look closely at his own wife. The proof is the word 'now': if אברהם only 'now' knew שרה was beautiful, he had not looked at her before.

keyTerms.meaning: I made a covenant with my eyes
we can learn from this that

phrases.english: "I made a covenant with my eyes,
phrases.notes: איוב 31:1

phrases.english: so how could I look at a young woman?"
Rava said: Dust in the mouth of איוב!
He did not look at other women,
but Abraham did not look even at his own wife,
as it is written: "Now I know
phrases.notes: בראשית 12:11

phrases.english: that you are a beautiful woman";

phrases.aramaic: מִכְּלָל דְּמֵעִיקָּרָא לָא הֲוָה יָדַע לַהּ.
phrases.english: which shows that before then he did not know it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third criticism in the same 'dust in איוב's mouth' pattern, this time from רבא and with a proof from a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: אברהם did not even look at his own wife.
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית 12:11, where 'now I know' shows he did not know before.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: איוב's boast was small compared to אברהם's level of holiness in what he looked at.

steps.title: רבא says איוב denied תחיית המתים
steps.stepSummary: From איוב's words that one who goes down to the grave will not come up, רבא learns that איוב denied תחיית המתים.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'As a cloud fades and is gone, so one who goes down to the grave will not come up.' רבא said: From here we see that איוב denied תחיית המתים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא reads another פסוק of איוב and draws a serious conclusion about what איוב believed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A cloud that disappears never comes back. איוב compares a dead person to that cloud, so רבא understands that איוב did not believe the dead will rise again.

phrases.english: "As a cloud fades and is gone,
phrases.notes: איוב 7:9

phrases.english: so one who goes down to the grave will not come up":

steps.title: רבה says איוב spoke against Heaven with a storm and was answered with a storm
steps.stepSummary: איוב complained that ה׳ crushes him 'with a storm.' רבה says איוב spoke against Heaven with a storm and was answered with a storm.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'For He crushes me with a storm, and adds to my wounds for no reason.' רבה said: איוב blasphemed with a storm, and with a storm they answered him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה reads another of איוב's complaints and points out a measure-for-measure link: the same 'storm' theme comes back in the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: איוב used the image of a storm to complain against ה׳. רבה says the answer he received matched his words, also coming with a storm.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: איוב complained using the image of a storm, and he was answered with a storm, measure for measure.

steps.title: How איוב spoke against Heaven with a storm
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the first half of רבה's statement. איוב said ה׳ crushes him 'with a storm,' and suggested a storm made ה׳ confuse איוב with אויב.
steps.simpleTranslation: He spoke against Heaven with a storm, as it is written: 'He who crushes me with a storm.' He said before Him: Master of the world, perhaps a stormy wind passed before You, and You mixed up איוב and אויב (enemy)?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is filling in what רבה meant when he said איוב 'spoke against Heaven with a storm.' It quotes איוב's פסוק and spells out his complaint.
steps.deeperAnalysis: איוב's complaint was that ה׳ treats him like an enemy by mistake. He blamed the mix-up on a storm, which suggests that ה׳'s judgment could get confused. That idea is what makes it חירוף, speaking against Heaven.

phrases.english: He spoke against Heaven with a storm, as it is written:
"He who crushes me with a storm";
phrases.notes: איוב 9:17. Here the word is spelled with a ש, just like the word for 'hair.' Keep that in mind for ה׳'s answer.

phrases.english: He said before Him: Master of the world,
perhaps a stormy wind passed before You,
and You got mixed up between איוב and an enemy?
phrases.notes: אִיּוֹב and אוֹיֵב are spelled with almost the same letters, so they look and sound alike.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first half of רבה's statement in Step 31.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: איוב's 'storm' complaint was a claim that ה׳ confused איוב with אויב.

steps.title: ה׳ answered איוב from the storm
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the פסוק showing that ה׳ answered איוב 'from the storm,' which is the second half of רבה's statement.
steps.simpleTranslation: He was answered with a storm, as it is written: 'And ה׳ answered איוב from the storm and said: [etc.] Gird your loins now like a man, I will ask you and you let Me know.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the second half of רבה's words: איוב was answered 'with a storm.' This step also sets up the content of ה׳'s answer, which comes in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer matches the complaint exactly. איוב mentioned a storm, so ה׳ answered him from the storm. The next steps explain what that 'storm' answer actually said.

phrases.english: He was answered with a storm, as it is written:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation of רבה's statement by proving the 'answered with a storm' half.

steps.raayaSupportSource: איוב 38:1, 'And ה׳ answered איוב from the storm'

steps.title: ה׳'s first answer: every hair has its own follicle
steps.stepSummary: ה׳ tells איוב that He gave each hair its own follicle so a person's eyesight won't be harmed. If He never confuses follicles, He would not confuse איוב with אויב.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I created many hairs in a person, and for each hair I created its own follicle, so that two would not draw from one follicle. If two drew from one follicle, they would darken a person's eyesight. Between one follicle and another I don't get mixed up; between איוב and אויב I would get mixed up?!
steps.whatsHappening: ה׳ gives His first answer to איוב's complaint, using the example of hair. This is the meaning of 'from the storm' (סערה sounds like שערה, a hair).
steps.deeperAnalysis: ה׳ points to something tiny: each hair has its own exact place, and a mix-up there would cause real harm. If He is this exact with tiny hairs, it makes no sense that He would mix up two people. The question 'would I mix up איוב and אויב?!' is a strong rhetorical rejection of איוב's claim.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳'s exact care for every hair shows He could never confuse איוב with אויב.

steps.title: ה׳'s second answer: every raindrop has its own channel
steps.stepSummary: Using a פסוק from ה׳'s speech, the גמרא explains that each raindrop has its own channel so the land won't be ruined. Again: if ה׳ doesn't confuse drops, He won't confuse איוב with אויב.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Who split a channel for the flood [etc.]': I created many drops in the clouds, and for each drop I created its own mold, so that two drops would not come out of one mold. If two drops came out of one mold, they would wash away the earth and it would not produce fruit. Between one drop and another I don't get mixed up; between איוב and אויב I would get mixed up?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second example of the same argument, this time from rain, based on a פסוק in ה׳'s answer to איוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pattern is the same as the hair example. Each drop has its own exact path, and a mix-up would destroy the crops. This repeats the point: ה׳ is exact even with tiny things.

keyTerms.meaning: A flood, a strong rush of water
A mold or form that something comes out of

steps.title: How do we know תעלה means a channel?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pauses to ask how we know the word תעלה in the פסוק means a mold or channel.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where is it implied that this word תעלה means a mold?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a side question about the meaning of a word. This sets up the proof that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The raindrop explanation depends on reading תעלה as a separate channel for each drop. The גמרא wants a source showing the word can carry that meaning.

steps.title: רבה בר שילא proves תעלה means a channel
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר שילא brings a פסוק where תעלה clearly means a trench or channel.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר שילא said: As it is written, 'And he made a channel the size of an area for sowing two סאה of seed.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר שילא answers the word question with a פסוק where תעלה means a dug-out channel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In that פסוק, a תעלה is a trench dug around something, so the word means a channel. That supports reading ה׳'s words as describing a separate channel for each drop.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: תעלה means a channel, as in the פסוק 'And he made a תעלה' (מלכים א 18:32).

steps.title: ה׳'s third answer: every thunderclap has its own path
steps.stepSummary: From the second half of the same פסוק, ה׳ explains that each thunderclap has its own path so the world won't be destroyed. If He doesn't confuse thunderclaps, He won't confuse איוב with אויב.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And a path for the lightning of thunder': I created many thunderclaps in the clouds, and for each one I created its own path, so that two thunderclaps would not come out of one path. If two came out of one path, they would destroy the whole world. Between one thunderclap and another I don't get mixed up; between איוב and אויב I would get mixed up?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns from the side question and gives the third and final example, thunder, using the second half of the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The stakes grow with each example: hair affects a person's eyes, rain affects the land, and thunder could destroy the whole world. Each time the conclusion is the same: ה׳ is exact in every detail, so איוב's claim of a mix-up is impossible.
steps.whatToRemember: איוב claimed a 'storm' made ה׳ confuse איוב with אויב. ה׳ answered 'from the storm' with three examples: hair, raindrops and thunder. Each has its own exact place, so ה׳ never confuses anything, and certainly not people.

steps.title: The wild goat that is cruel to her young
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a פסוק from ה׳'s speech about the wild goat giving birth. It begins to explain that this goat is cruel to her young at the moment she crouches to give birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Do you know the time when the wild goats of the rock give birth? Can you watch over the birthing of the hinds?" This wild goat is cruel to her young. When she crouches to give birth...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new example from ה׳'s speech to איוב, this time about the wild goat. It is setting up a detailed explanation that continues in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the hair follicles, raindrops, and thunderclaps, this is another case where ה׳ watches over a tiny detail of nature. The new piece of information here is that the יעלה is cruel to her young as she gives birth. This sets up how ה׳ steps in to protect them, and the point will again be that ה׳ never confuses איוב with אויב.
